Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-15-0**

### Highlights

- **Link aggregation done right** (#145) - an aggregate is an interface of type LAG carrying the bundle settings: protocol (static / LACP / PAgP), LACP mode and rate, min links. Members may sit on any member of the same virtual chassis, so a stack's port-channel lives once on the master. The LAG picker offers aggregates only with an inline *New aggregate*; the interface table gains a LAG column; the aggregate's page has a Bundle card (capacity, peer aggregates, min-links verdict), a Members tab and its members' cable runs; a member's page carries a *Member of Po1 · LACP active* chip; the device overview groups a bundle's runs; topology folds member cables into one thick edge (Display → Bundle aggregates). SNMP discovery reads membership (LAG-MIB, ifStackTable fallback), creates aggregates typed LAG and reports `lag_membership` drift; sync applies it.
- **IP ranges as allocation pools** (#143) - adding an IP inside a subnet that holds ranges offers a Range field: what's free, one-click picks, a Next free button, a nudge when the address falls outside. The range page's Addresses tab is the ordinary IP table cut to the span, free rows click-to-add, with a Compact fold the prefix IPs tab has too. **Allocate only from ranges** on a prefix makes the ranges its whole allocatable space - for a provider's slice of a subnet that isn't yours: next available walks the ranges, Show available and Add pool offer only range addresses, utilisation counts against the ranges' size (*Used 1 of 7 · Free 6*), the IP form requires a Range pick, and the API refuses a new address outside every range.
- **Antennas** (#111) - a dedicated antenna component and device-type template with structured RF fields: gain in dBi, multi-select bands, polarization, RF connector, direct-mount flag. RF connector types join the aux-port vocabulary, so an AP to external antenna coax run is an ordinary cable. Antennas get their own pane on the device Hardware tab, ride along in bundle export/import, and faceplates draw RF slugs as antenna stubs.
- **Circuit terminations cable like ports** (#118) - the provider handoff cables to the switch port it lands on, with a Device/Circuit toggle on each cable end. Traces and the device Paths tab run out to the demarc; the circuit page's termination card shows *Cabled to*.
- **Interface lifecycle status** (#105) - Active / Disabled / Planned / Not present / Decommissioning on every interface, set by SNMP sync where it applies, respected by utilization and monitoring, with bulk edit and filters.
- **Sync a device type's whole fleet** (#103) - preview, a warning step that counts what gets removed (red when interfaces carrying IPs are among it), then a background run with progress and per-device permission re-checks.
- **GeoJSON / QGIS boundary import** (#80) - upload a region boundary; WGS84 enforced (projected exports refused with a reproject hint), multi-feature files merge, Douglas-Peucker simplification trims the shape until it fits, with a report of what that cost.
- **Every edit form on the sectioned card layout** (#78) - two columns where they earn them, colored pickers everywhere a table shows a badge, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter saves, dialogs grow to fit their content instead of scrolling sideways, custom-field groups as their own cards.
- **Device-type import for air-gapped servers** - a *Fetch with my browser* tick on the devicetype-library import: your browser downloads the YAML and sends it up, so the server never has to reach GitHub.

### IPAM & records

- **Custom-field values are searchable** - the global search bar and every list's filter box match inside custom fields, so an imported NetBox id finds its object. **Custom-field definitions can be hidden** - the value stays on the object and in search, but no card, table, popover or form shows it; the NetBox importer creates its `netbox_id` / `netbox_tenant` definitions hidden.
- **Speeds given as bare kbps read as the dropdown's form** - a scraper writing `1000000` lands as `1G` (`25000000` → `25G`, `1234000` → `1.234G`) on save through the API, the form, bulk edit and VM interfaces; anything with a unit is kept as typed. Migration `api.0154` rewrites rows already stored that way.
- **Working hours on contacts** (#66) and **provider support details** (#67) - a shared weekly schedule (multiple spans per day, time zone required), an *Open now* readout, and provider fields for support contract, support phone and an account manager.
- **SSID pre-shared keys live in the secret store** (#68) - write-only on the form, revealed only through a separate audited action behind its own grant, fail-closed when no store is configured.
- **VM interfaces get a type** (#140) - Virtual, Tunnel (WireGuard/GRE/VXLAN/tun), Bridge or Loopback - and **nest** under a parent interface on the same VM.
- **VM primary IP from the address form** (#122); **aggregate pages list their prefixes** (#133) with a `contained_in=<cidr>` prefix filter; VLAN prefixes assignable straight from the VLAN page; site time zone as a dropdown (#120); searchable custom-field rule pickers (#113); custom fields on 12 more detail pages incl. virtual chassis (#114); restored Add/Import buttons (#112).
- **Name ranges expand server-side** - `eth[1-4]` fans out in one request on ports, templates and components alike, atomically.
- **Statuses list shows the colour value** - a swatch and the hex next to the badge, sortable.
- **Short ids are searchable** - an all-digit query matches the number printed on labels across every type, and cables join global search. **Search puts the closest match first** (#138) - exact, then prefix, then substring, in the IP list and every combobox.

### DCIM

- **Photo ports per device, printed labels, stable markers** - a device can override its type's photo-port layout (Photo ports tab, Reset to type layout); interfaces and front/rear ports carry a printed label shown in tables, hovers and traces; ports keep a frozen marker identity so renaming never orphans a photo marker; the editor fits the image and zooms, and *Use this size everywhere* makes the device page's photo panel draw at that size instead of the column's full width.
- **Faceplates** - a deployment setting lights up ports marked connected like cabled ones, drawn in their speed tier; the photo-port hover carries the same configurable rows as the drawn faceplate (name and label, type, state, VLAN badge, live SNMP state, IPs); rendered faceplates no longer print the interface prefix before each port group (it pushed dense panels past their card) - Settings → Admin → Faceplates turns it back on.
- **Bulk-renaming component templates follows into photo markers, faceplate slots and placed ports** like a single rename does. Before, the markers kept the old names and sync-from-type stamped them again as bare *Other* interfaces on every device of the type; `api.0155` repairs types already in that state.
- **Virtual chassis** - the list shows the members' combined status (one badge when they agree, a split of the distinct colours when they don't) and a merged monitoring rollup, with a Status facet in the rail; the edit form has Tags; the page carries a stack-wide port utilization card and the members' live check badges; the virtual topology scrolls inside a viewport-high box.
- **Add device from a site** (#134); **disconnect a cable from the interface list** (#137); **interface VLAN pickers put the device's site first** (#136); adding an IP from a device/VM interface pre-selects its site (#135).
- **Cable form port panel** (#130) - long interface prefixes truncate with a hover reveal, the panel gets a Hide toggle, and an already-cabled port is flagged in the picker (#121).
- **Device photos downscale on upload** (2000px longest edge, EXIF rotation applied); rack-face images get a Resize control; **device-type documents carry to every device** read-only under *From device type*; the rack Assign dialog places half-width devices.
- **Cable labels get bare port names** - `a_port_name` / `b_port_name` tokens.

### Floor plans, maps & 3D

- **Floor plans clone** with everything drawn on them; a tile's type or role changes from the inspector; the tile popover shows the uploaded front / rear photo when that side has no ports mapped and lays its rows out striped; **Show on floor plan** zooms onto the tile, with a menu when the object sits on several plans.
- **Faceplate popovers** (#102) - a device-linked tile draws the box's front/rear panel in its hover popover.
- Tiles redrawn with a seam and calmer outlines; 3D devices carry a camera-facing name tag; 3D walls no longer vanish when switching shell mode or render quality.

### Monitoring & integrations

- **SNMP source-of-truth policies** - update-only (never add interfaces), skip unrouted L2 VLAN rows, take the MAC from the forwarding table, grouped-VLAN VID matching, a default VRF for discovered addresses per device / role / type / site / tenant. Pre-allocated stack interfaces are no longer added as active (#97).
- **Poll now routes through the site's Outpost** (#128); the Outpost-offline window is configurable per tenant (#129).
- **Monitoring settings get their own tab** (#63); switch-link suggestion ARP sources persist (#127).
- **Windows DHCP lease sync survives non-MAC ClientIds** (#115); **virt sync can match existing VLANs by ID** (#116), migrating networks that minted their own VLAN; adopted VMs surface spec drift for review instead of auto-applying.

### Access & sign-in

- **Hide local login behind a link** (#119) - SSO buttons lead, *sign in with a local account* reveals the form, `/login?local=1` deep-links it, fails open with no enabled provider.
- **grant_superuser as a permission verb** - a user-admin can set or clear superuser without being one; every flip audited. **A tenant-scoped grant is tenant access** - no second manual membership step.

### Everyday interface

- **The sidebar shows where you are** and sits tighter: 24px rows, a primary bar on the active category's band, a rail down the cluster holding the current page.
- **Tables: badges sort and filter on click** - status / VLAN / role headers sort everywhere, sort headers show their direction, and a tag chip or an enum badge in a cell toggles that filter in the rail, on every list with a rail; the Monitoring rollup badge on devices and prefixes is a facet too, and sorts; the rails draw facets with the shared badge.
- **Every page names its browser tab**; docs gain a front-nginx example and WebSocket troubleshooting for Docker (#146).
- Circuit dates use the calendar picker, long select values truncate with a hover reveal (#124), tooltips stopped inverting in dark mode, the advanced filter's value list scrolls (#117), docs links survive a missing trailing slash (#123), dark-theme surface colours are consistent between pages (#52).

### Fixes

- **Site SNMP and engine bindings stopped disappearing** (#125) - two causes: site-scoped users were refused the profile catalog so the select rendered empty, and browser autofill fired change events on the form's hidden native selects that the save-on-change controls persisted; changes without a user gesture are ignored and the controls stay disabled until loaded.
- **Clicking a MAC no longer 500s on VM-polling tenants** (#139); sightings name the device or the VM.
- **Device pages stay inside the viewport** (#132); trace segments make room for the link-icon glyph; the IP form keeps a subnet you picked when narrowing to its own site.
- Overview is reachable again on a page whose pinned default tab is another one - clicking it dropped the tab from the URL and the page fell back to the pin.
- Change-log filters survive back navigation (#109), saved views split from the Devices list (#107), the site map can't be squeezed to nothing (#108), serializers that override validate() no longer skip base validation (#106), logical-view.tsx is diffable again (#110), SSH terminal gate tests are order-independent (#81).

### Upgrading

- Migrations apply automatically: interface status seed, antennas, business hours, SSID PSK references, hide-local-login, VLAN matching, the circuit-termination cable point, device-type run kinds, LAG fields (`api.0153` promotes untyped aggregates that already have members to type LAG), kbps speed normalisation (`api.0154`), the photo-marker repair (`api.0155`), allocate-from-ranges (`api.0156`), the faceplate settings (`core.0046`, `core.0047`), hidden custom fields (`customization.0006`), SNMP policies (`monitoring.0079`–`0081`).
- LAG membership now requires the target to be type LAG; an importer must create aggregates typed LAG before members. Outposts report LAG membership once their vendored `danbyte_checks` is synced; older agents keep working without membership drift.
- Rendered faceplates hide the interface prefix by default; Settings → Admin → Faceplates → *Show interface prefixes on rendered faceplates* restores it.
- The devicetype-library browser fetch needs `raw.githubusercontent.com` and `api.github.com` in nginx's `connect-src`; the shipped template has them, a hand-written config must add them. The #123 docs-redirect fix (`proxy_redirect / /docs/;`) likewise only reaches existing installs when their nginx config is regenerated or patched.
